reason: I ask ChatGPT questions, but I make the trades myself, and that's on purpose. I'm 53 with less than $20k put away, so I'm not handing an AI pet the keys to real money, even with limits.
objection: If the AI makes a bad call on its own, it's my retirement money that's gone, and a downloadable record of what went wrong doesn't give it back. Plus it's a new app, the broker isn't even named yet, and they want a monthly fee for it.
would_change_my_mind: If it only suggested trades and I had to approve every single one, through a big licensed broker I already know, with my account insured, and a year of watching it on the demo money do better than I do on my own.
